paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God is not finished with Israel, and He is not finished with you. Paul says "God's gifts and His call are irrevocable" (Romans 11:29). That means when God makes a promise, He keeps it, even when people stumble, and even when it takes a long time.

Now look at how Paul says God works. He says God "has consigned everyone to disobedience so that He may have mercy on everyone" (Romans 11:32). Nobody gets to stand over anybody else, Gentile or Israel, because every one of us is held up by mercy. That's why Paul opens by warning the Gentiles not to be conceited (Romans 11:25). A mercy you were handed is nothing to brag about.

So when you can't figure out what God is doing, do what Paul does. He doesn't solve it, he worships: "How unsearchable are His judgments, and untraceable His ways!" (Romans 11:33). Nobody has ever given God a thing first, and nobody has ever been His counselor (Romans 11:34-35). "For from Him and through Him and to Him are all things. To Him be the glory forever! Amen." (Romans 11:36). Trust Him, baker, and give Him the glory.
